title: Tenant and Customer User Management
baseline: IBeam Management 2.15.0; original Management API epic is shipped. This is a new follow-on epic, not a reopening of completed work.

common.architecture: Portal API -> Management services -> scoped HTTPS client -> target Identity Management API -> Identity management services -> existing Identity services/stores or entity-focused repositories. Custom service operations execute through IServiceOperationExecutor. Customer Identity is registered only in the target app; the support host retains its isolated identity realm.
common.safety: Every operation requires an enabled app connection, live support assignment, independent human operation permission, target machine capability and target host policy. ac: Both new packages build/pack independently; core and portal packages do not acquire a dependency on customer IBeam.Identity or on the support Identity adapter.
No target customer routes or customer capabilities are registered without explicit opt-in; authentication defaults and existing customer routes remain unchanged.

IBM-0098 (TCM-001), 5 points: optional customer Identity target foundation.

Added IBeam.Management.Identity.Target.Services and .Api packages with explicit registration, target-only named machine authentication, live credential/app/environment/version checks, stable dedicated Identity realm configuration and version-1 GET /api/management-identity/info. Discovery-only management.identity.info credentials are independently issued through existing trusted tooling; this does not grant customer directory/provisioning access. Merely referencing the assembly adds no routes.

Added provider-neutral typed module metadata, safe tenant/user DTOs and bounded directory ports to IBeam.Management. Portal/core keep no customer Identity or support Identity dependencies. Added opt-in GET /api/management/applications/{applicationId}/customer-management, requiring a live enabled app connection and existing operation assignment even for administrators. Returns only last-verified metadata, never customer data or secret material.

Independent IManagementTargetProfileProbe supports Identity-only (diagnostics 404), existing diagnostics-only and combined targets. Exact app/environment/realm/protocol validation; unknown/malformed/oversized customer metadata disables customer availability while preserving valid diagnostics. Existing strict diagnostic sanitization parser, constructors/interfaces, outbound approved HTTPS/DNS/IP pinning/TLS policy and authentication defaults remain unchanged. Added optional typed Azure Table connection metadata column without migrating legacy rows or granting new permissions. New metadata-only audit operations cover the target and portal services.

Validation: 388 tests passed, zero failed/skipped: Management 34, credential 61, diagnostics 150, applications 108 (including new portal checks and real isolated Table round trips), customer Identity discovery 35. Covered old constructors/legacy rows, connection rotation, mismatched bindings, independent version negotiation, unsafe/malformed metadata, named-auth substitution, missing/revoked/expired machine credentials, route opt-in, unsupported/missing realm configuration, no-adapter capability suppression, active assignment revocation, app/organization isolation and payload-free audit. cards.verification:
IBM-0099 (TCM-002), 5 points: independent customer operations, delegation ceilings and effective capability projection.

Extended machine credential validation/provisioning and human app assignments with thirteen independently recognized management.identity customer operations, excluding discovery from human assignment. Existing diagnostic credentials/rows remain unchanged and receive no new authority. Composite users.provision requires invites.manage and roles.assign; onboarding.create additionally requires tenants.create, invites.manage and roles.assign; onboarding.retry also requires onboarding.create. Direct application-access and portal authorization services enforce this matrix through IServiceOperationExecutor.

Customer delegation claims require the exact operation and application ID, plus live support administrator/access-admin checks. Both old and requested assignment permissions are checked for update/revoke; self-assignment has the same ceiling. Built-in support Identity adds explicit trusted CustomerDelegations configuration for named user/app/operation bindings, default empty. MFA enrichment and each live JWT validation regenerate claims from current validated options and live membership; stale token permission/role claims are removed. Public old constructors and RefreshPrincipal overload remain available. Invalid/wildcard/duplicate binding configuration fails closed.

Target EnabledOperations is an explicit default-empty ceiling; discovery intersects machine capabilities, enabled policy and installed/resolving adapters, including composite prerequisites. Selector and customer-management discovery expose only effective assigned supported operations, including Identity-only apps. New IManagementCustomerIdentityAuthorizationService validates the full matrix without resolving keys or accessing customer storage. Target module/policy metadata remains a last-verified connection snapshot; future data routes must also enforce live target policy/credential plus the verified delegated actor delivered by IBM-0100.

Validation: 491 unique tests passed across customer Identity 40, applications 131, support Identity 74, credentials 62, Management foundation 34 and diagnostics 150. No failed or outstanding skipped cases. The first support Identity run had its separate-store fixture unavailable (73 passed / 1 skipped); supplying the second local emulator and rerunning both storage modes passed both cases. Covered all 13 operation matrices, composite missing prerequisites, wrong-app/per-operation delegation, self-assignment denial without authority, old diagnostic assignments, direct authorization, disabled users, changed connections, revoked grants, Identity-only selector output, effective permission filtering, default-empty/invalid host policy, missing adapters, explicit target capabilities, key rotation/revocation and support role/configured-ceiling refresh.

Builds and local validation packs use 2.16.0-dev.tcm.99. Documents explain the operation/delegation matrix, target policy, configuration reload/restart behavior and no automatic upgrades. No customer data endpoints, impersonation, frontend, production deployment or manual publishing.

cards.verification:
IBM-0100 (TCM-003), 5 points: verified support actor delegation.

Added IManagementDelegatedActorProvider, validator/context/target-access ports, short-lived server-only actor assertion wrappers and exact request binding. Portal issuance rechecks live app/human grants and active connection, obtains the actual machine credential ID from the scoped secret, and signs RS256 with a host-supplied dedicated RSA key. Explicit issuer and per-app audience configuration, maximum 60-second lifetime (default 30), named key IDs and no default production keys. Assertion, request body/path and key values are never serialized as DTO/audit content.

Optional target delegation installs an explicit support-organization/application/issuer/audience trust map, pinned public-key provider and scoped verified actor context. Rejects wrong/expired/future/overlong/ambiguous assertions, algorithm/type/key substitution, token-driven key URLs, mismatched app/environment/Identity realm/machine credential/operation/method/path/query/body. Current machine credential/version/expiry, target enabled operations and installed adapters remain independent gates. The API operation comes only from server endpoint metadata. Machine-only GET /info remains compatible; future customer endpoints require both dedicated headers and bound human proof. Direct target services require verified context and recheck current authority. No customer principal, membership or token is created for support actors.

Added atomic Azure Table replay claims for mutations with issuer/realm/assertion scope, bounded lifetime and explicit schema setup. Storage failures deny access. Trusted bounded maintenance refuses live/future cutoffs; documentation makes clear Azure Table has no automatic TTL and expired-row cleanup is an operator responsibility. Retrying a mutation needs a fresh assertion plus the same future business idempotency key. Read assertions remain usable only to signed expiry; grant revocation prevents new assertions and in-flight behavior is documented.

Audit sink preserves verified support organization/person, portal app and target machine credential separately with safe correlation, no raw assertions/payload/hash/profile/exception text. Existing sink constructor is preserved. Repeated connection/target registrations are now idempotent so composing modules does not append duplicated configuration arrays. Startup validates required signing/validation/replay/audit dependencies.

Validation: 521 tests passed, zero failed/skipped: customer Identity/delegation 69, applications 132, support Identity 74 (both storage modes), credentials 62, Management 34, diagnostics 150. Covers real signed HTTP calls, 20 substitution cases, malformed signed metadata/remote-key header, key removal, human/machine/policy revocation, no-context direct calls, separate audit identities, assertion redaction, concurrent HTTP replay, fresh retry, real Table cross-instance atomic claims and bounded cleanup, plus existing auth/assignment/diagnostic regressions. Fixed embedded-host encoded path fallback and JsonIgnore/required wrapper serialization before the final run.

Packed and inspected five affected Management packages at local validation version 2.16.0-dev.tcm.100 for expected DLL/README/icon/agent guidance and absence of fixture controllers, local configs/logs/debug artifacts. No customer directory/provisioning routes, frontend, production resources or manual NuGet publishing. This completes TCM-F01 (IBM-0098 through IBM-0100), 15 points.

Persist request fingerprints, deterministic reserved resource IDs, step/status, versions, safe result references, actor/credential/correlation and mutation audit intent. Add IManagementIdentityOperationService and GET /api/management-identity/operations/{operationId}, mirrored by the portal. Schema creation is explicit trusted setup.
ac: Idempotency-Key is mandatory for mutating customer-management requests; scope includes support organization, target realm/app, operation and resource, with a canonical payload fingerprint.
Same key and same request returns the existing operation/result; same key with changed request returns 409; concurrent requests cannot reserve duplicate work.
Operation rows use atomic claims/ETags and stable resource IDs; a crash after a downstream write resumes or reconciles that write instead of blindly creating it again.
Safe audit intent is persisted before a mutation; inability to record it prevents a new mutation, and persisted outbox-style events can be delivered without repeating customer changes.
Receipts contain no raw request bodies, email/password/invite secrets or customer profiles; retention, idempotency expiry and safe polling limits are documented.
Operation reads require the original write authority or explicit onboarding.read as appropriate plus app scope; unrelated apps/organizations cannot enumerate or retrieve receipts.

cards.scope: Add IManagementTenantAdministrationService with POST /api/management-identity/tenants and PATCH /tenants/{tenantId}. Add ManagementTenantAdministrationEntity metadata only for source (support-provisioned/unknown), external reference and operation linkage; existing/self-signup tenants remain unknown unless a trusted consumer reports provenance. ac: Create validates bounded name/optional external reference, reserves a stable tenant ID and creates exactly one tenant through Identity services; duplicate external references follow an explicit target-scoped uniqueness policy.
Support creation returns only tenant metadata/operation reference and grants the operator no customer membership, customer role, token or default tenant.
Rename requires tenants.update and the returned version/If-Match; missing or stale versions cannot silently overwrite another change.

Legacy tenant rows are not rewritten on reads; provenance never infers self-signup from missing metadata and arbitrary consumer profile fields are rejected.

cards.scope: Add POST /api/management/applications/{applicationId}/tenants and PATCH /tenants/{tenantId}, with operation polling under /operations/{operationId}. features.title: Enterprise onboarding and first administrator invitation
features.outcome: Provide one recoverable operation to create an enterprise tenant and invite its first customer administrator. The customer accepts through the application's own Identity flow and signs in normally.
acceptance: One enterprise onboarding request creates one tenant and one recoverable administrator invitation.
Customer ownership and password/email verification stay in the application's established Identity acceptance flow.
Partial completion and uncertain email delivery are visible and safely recoverable.

cards.title: Orchestrate enterprise tenant and initial administrator invitation
cards.scope: Add IManagementEnterpriseOnboardingService. Request includes tenant name, initial admin email, optional external reference and a server-approved onboarding policy key. Use the operation journal to reserve tenant/invite IDs and coordinate tenant creation, extension completion, invitation creation/delivery and owner acceptance status. Reuse ITenantInviteService through a management-aware external actor adapter; do not pass a support user GUID as a fictitious customer inviter. Durable invite identity/delivery deduplication must be added where existing APIs cannot reconcile after crashes.
ac: Onboarding requires onboarding.create plus tenants.create, invites.manage and approved roles.assign authority on both human and target credentials; direct service calls cannot bypass composite checks.
One idempotent request creates one tenant and one pending initial-admin invitation; retries after each crash point reuse the same tenant/invitation instead of creating duplicates.
Admin/Owner role templates are host-allowlisted and target-local; arbitrary role names, support roles, wildcard permissions or caller-provided redirect URLs are rejected.
New and existing customer identities must satisfy the existing verified recipient/password-setup acceptance flow; management never sets/returns passwords or grants support staff customer membership.

Status distinguishes tenant creation, extension completion, invitation persisted, delivery sent/failed/unknown, awaiting acceptance, completed and recoverable failure; sending an email alone never marks onboarding complete.
Delivery failure does not delete the tenant or create another invitation automatically; explicit retry/resend reconciles invitation state and records possible at-least-once email delivery.
Existing self-signup routes remain available and unchanged; pending onboarding never grants customer access before the intended administrator has valid tenant membership.

features.title: Tenant and membership access lifecycle
features.outcome: Allow authorized operators to disable/reactivate a tenant or manage one customer's membership and permitted roles. Changes are limited to the selected tenant and prevent last-administrator lockout.
acceptance: Tenant status and customer membership/role operations are independently authorized and audited.
Membership changes do not globally disable the customer or alter other tenants.
Concurrent operations cannot remove the last eligible administrator or bypass access revocation.

cards.title: Manage tenant membership status and approved roles without global account changes
cards.scope: Add PATCH /tenants/{tenantId}/users/{userId}/membership for isEnabled and PUT /tenants/{tenantId}/users/{userId}/roles for approved role IDs, target and portal mirrors. IManagementCustomerMembershipService calls existing role/membership services through additive versioned ports where needed. Preserve global account state and default-tenant semantics; no password reset, MFA reset, delete or impersonation endpoints.
ac: Membership enable/disable requires memberships.manage; role changes require roles.assign and the approved target-local role catalog.
Both operations require expected versions and idempotency, are serialized/guarded per tenant where needed, and cannot disable/demote the final eligible administrator under concurrent requests.
Disabling a membership preserves the customer's global account and other memberships; re-enable never restores privileges that were separately removed.
Effective access is rejected at customer tenant authorization/refresh boundaries with documented bounded revocation semantics; a test covers an already-issued customer token.
Rejected or partially completed changes leave a reconcilable operation/audit result and never silently report success; reasons use bounded safe codes without arbitrary sensitive free text.
Cross-app/tenant IDs, privilege escalation, stale versions, multi-tenant accounts and concurrent last-administrator changes are covered by service and provider tests.
